steps.title: Why indexes exist
steps.content: An index is a data structure that helps the database find rows without scanning every row in a table. It can speed up reads, but it uses storage and may slow inserts, updates and deletes because the index must also be maintained.
steps.example: An index on Employee(employee_id) helps look up an employee by ID.

steps.title: Choose an indexing candidate
steps.prompt: Which query is most likely to benefit from an index on email?
steps.explanation: The equality predicate searches for rows by email, so an index on email can help locate them.

steps.title: Understand composite indexes
steps.content: A composite index contains more than one column. Column order matters because many database engines can use the leftmost prefix of the index efficiently.
steps.example: An index on (department_id, salary) can help queries filtering by department_id, and often by both department_id and salary.

steps.title: Recognize a trigger
options: Code automatically invoked by a specified database event
steps.explanation: A trigger runs automatically when its configured event occurs, such as an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.

steps.title: Before and after triggers
steps.content: A BEFORE trigger runs before the data change; an AFTER trigger runs after it. Triggers can enforce rules or maintain audit records, but hidden side effects make them harder to debug.
steps.tip: Use triggers deliberately and document their effects on related tables.

questions.prompt: What is a main benefit of an index?
questions.explanation: Indexes can reduce the amount of data read to find matching rows.

questions.prompt: What is a common cost of maintaining indexes?
questions.explanation: Indexes occupy storage and must be updated when indexed values change.

questions.prompt: A trigger is commonly activated by:
options: A defined INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE event
questions.explanation: Database triggers respond to specified database events.

questions.prompt: When does an AFTER trigger run?
questions.explanation: An AFTER trigger executes after the triggering operation.
